title: The additive ideal image is the pushforward of the relative additive kernel.
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and J ≤ I quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Write i_J: Z_J → X and j: Z_I → Z_J. For the additive restriction r [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction] and direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], the categorical image of ker(r_I) → A_X → (i_J)_*A_Z_J is isomorphic to (i_J)_* ker(r_j). No nilpotence or square-zero hypothesis is required.

proof.text: On affine etale objects over affine X-opens, the additive kernel before restriction is I_B. The relative kernel of B/J_B → B/I_B is I_B/J_B, and every class in it has a representative in I_B. Thus the additive image and relative kernel coincide on this affine basis, compatibly with all restrictions.

Direct image preserves kernels. Use the base-change composition isomorphism and j followed by i_J equals i_I to view its kernel inclusion as a monomorphism into the target of the displayed composite. The affine representative argument gives a locally surjective factorization through this subobject.

Sheafifying the sectionwise image gives the categorical image in abelian sheaves. Hence the preceding factorization is an image factorization. Uniqueness gives the isomorphism, with the same coefficient universe lift as in the additive sheaf.

theorem nonempty_idealAdditiveImageRelativeKernelIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    (I J : X.IdealSheafData) (hJI : J ≤ I) :
    Nonempty (image (kernel.ι (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar I.subschemeι) ≫
        etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar J.subschemeι) ≅
      (Etale.lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} J.subschemeι).obj
        (kernel (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar (IdealSheafData.inclusion hJI))))
